newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee should fall to 37.7 by March - report.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee should fall to 37.7 by March - report.

text.p: The Indian rupee needs to fall to 37.7 against the dollar by March 1997 in order to maintain its real exchange rate, securities firm SocGen-Crosby said.
The Indian rupee would be under downward pressure in the next three months because of large outflows on the capital account and bunching of external debt payments, it said in a January report.
An industrial revival would also lead to increased imports.
It said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was aware of the threat to the local currency. It has been gradually building up its foreign exchange reserves to meet the debt repayments.

"Although the RBI wants the exchange rate to gradually depreciate in order to maintain the rupee close to its fair value, the RBI intervention will ensure that the currency does not fall below 37.7 against the dollar before end-March 97," the report said.
